note: BLM campground in the Alabama Hills foothills west of Lone Pine, in two rows of gravel spurs either side of Tuttle Creek. First come, first served. Potable water and the dump station are seasonal. Two sites come with a horse corral. --Claude
summary: Tuttle Creek: open all year, FCFS only (stored 'reservable on recreation.gov' was wrong), $12 credit card only, 83 sites, 30 ft recommended, ten pull-throughs; water and dump off until May 2027. Creekside KEPT (north-row sites 4-17 ~20-40 m from the creek). Two horse-corral sites share the loop (unnamed).
flags: BOOKING: stored reservable true -> false, fcfs always. BLM: 'No reservations.' rec.gov 10004620 is a first-come scan-and-pay listing (reservable none, every site reservable false). Only the group site is reservable, by phone.
FEES: stored $10 -> $12 (BLM page and rec.gov overview); rec.gov's $10 walk-in rate table disagrees, BLM's posted fee used.
STATUS: 'Water and Dump station are currently unavailable until May 2027.' (in status note; season year-round).

WATERFRONT: stored 'creekside' (not --AWH) KEPT. North row sites 4, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 13, 15, 16, 17 (e.g. site 15 at ~36.5651,-118.1262) end ~20-40 m from the centre of Tuttle Creek's ~20 m willow band over open sagebrush; the south row (52-68) is ~40-60 m. The channel itself is under willows, a small creek (well under 30 m), so creekside is the right value. All sites nightly, first come.

HORSE: 'Two horse corrals are available for $12.00 per night, including the associated site' - corral sites share the general loop and are not named on BLM or rec.gov; per the 2026-11-27 Wildcat ruling this is a keep with a caveat (note says two sites come with a corral). Not identified on imagery.
